clue.text: See walls in posh school explode

indicators.note: the first word's letters build walls round the school, enclosing it

parts.note: to see someone is to date them, as in a romance
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An alarming instruction to watch the walls of an exclusive school blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a looking verb here: it means go out with someone, DATE, which surrounds ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to make it explode; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Unknown individual in London band?

definitions.note: London's transport map is divided into concentric fare bands

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A mystery member of some London group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'band' is not musical: London's Underground fares are set by concentric zones, so the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport for London's fare areas are rings called zones, so one such band is a zone.

clue.text: Margaret, Lady Holroyd, losing daughter in crowd

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the novelist's surname

parts.note: the novelist Margaret Drabble is married to the biographer Michael Holroyd
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A titled woman, without her daughter, lost in a throng.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Holroyd is Dame Margaret Drabble, the novelist, by her husband's name; drop D from DRABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly mob of people, a kind of crowd.

clue.text: Excellent beer served up in Crown & Sceptre?

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 written as the letter I
lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Good beer being served in a pub called the Crown & Sceptre.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub name is really the definition: crown and sceptre are examples of royal insignia. A1 becomes AI, the digit standing in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty, such as the crown and sceptre used at a coronation.

clue.text: FM broadcast with time for transitory things

indicators.note: broadcast means the letters are spoken over the air, so we use their sound

parts.note: the letters F and M spoken one after the other, eff em
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A radio station's programming paired with a time slot for passing things.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letters F and M as names, 'eff-em', and they sound like the first syllables of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are items meant to last only a short while, like tickets or flyers, so they are fleeting.

clue.text: Drink and drive to accommodate a tense playwright

indicators.note: the two words make room for the next letters between them

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
an urge is a drive or impulse
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Advice to have a drink and drive over to put up a nervous dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the playwright, but it gives the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a dramatist, someone who writes or adapts works for the theatre.

clue.text: An obsessed person after exercise finds protein source

indicators.note: the obsessive comes after the exercise in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
taken as A
a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A gym fanatic, after a workout, finds something with protein in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are rich in protein, so a peanut is a source of it.

clue.text: Metal container for my French energy drink?

indicators.note: the metal is a container holding the French word

parts.note: lead is a metal
mon is French for my
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A metal can holding a French energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy drink' reads as one phrase; split it, as E ends the wordplay and drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink flavoured with lemons; the question mark admits the surface pairing with energy.

clue.text: Conference centre shunned by Herb

indicators.note: the herb's name avoids its own centre, the fourth of its seven letters, which is dropped

parts.note: parsley is a herb

explanation.surface: A meeting venue snubbed by a man called Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb looks like a man's name, but it is the plant; remove its central S.
explanation.definitionFit: A parley is a discussion or negotiation, especially between enemies, so a conference.

clue.text: He opposed the Reformation to a greater degree

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas ..., executed for refusing to accept Henry VIII as head of the Church

explanation.walkthrough: The first part describes a person: Thomas More, the Catholic chancellor who would not back Henry VIII's break with Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More resisted the English Reformation, and the word is also the plain comparative meaning further or extra.

clue.text: Code-breaker admittedly one talking wildly in British isle

indicators.note: the wild talker sits inside the British isle

parts.note: the Isle of Man
a raver is someone who raves, talking incoherently

explanation.surface: A cipher expert confessing to rambling on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: Suella Braverman resigned as Home Secretary in 2022 admitting she had breached the ministerial code, so she is a self-confessed code-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The politician owned up to breaking the ministerial rules of conduct, a topical allusion rather than a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Really good friend's introduced Buckingham say

indicators.note: the friend is introduced first, leading the word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A great mate has been brought in, perhaps a Mr Buckingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckingham Palace is the monarch's London residence, an example of a royal palace.

clue.text: Writing from hammer-wielder carried in gold vessel

indicators.note: the god is carried inside the gold and the vessel

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a ship is a vessel
Thor, the Norse god, wields the hammer Mjolnir

explanation.surface: An inscription telling of a hammer-wielding god borne in a golden ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The hammer-wielder is the Norse thunder god, whose hammer is Mjolnir.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorship is the act or occupation of writing books, so it can stand for writing.

clue.text: Distinct character, island god pens holy work

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: the god encloses the holy book, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: a deity is a god
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An island deity writing a sacred text has a distinctive personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity is the individuality that makes a person themselves, a distinct character.

clue.text: Material from Grobschnitt ultimately old hat

indicators.note: ultimately means take the very end of the German name

parts.note: ex means former, old
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Fabric from a German rock band in the end proves an old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Grobschnitt was a German rock band; only its last letter is used. Tile is dated British slang for a hat, as in a silk tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A textile is a woven or knitted fabric, so cloth material.

clue.text: Refuse to provide exits

definitions.meaning: first sense: the noun, leftover scraps or rubbish
second sense: departures, acts of leaving

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, decline, but it is the noun rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavings are leftover remains, and the plural of the noun from 'leave' also names departures.

clue.text: Sketch by artist showing struggle to survive

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to trace is to sketch an outline

explanation.surface: An artist's sketch depicting the fight to stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the artist next to the sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce competitive struggle of working life, fighting to get by.

clue.text: Note possible routes for traveller abandoned

parts.note: C is a musical note
a street and a way: A ST plus A WAY, two routes one might take

explanation.surface: A memo listing possible itineraries for a stranded traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible routes' breaks into A ST (a street) and A WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is a person left stranded after a shipwreck, an abandoned voyager.

clue.text: Exile concerned with stale atmosphere vacated enclosure

parts.note: re means about, concerning
fug is a stuffy, stale atmosphere in a room

indicators.note: emptied of its interior, so only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A banished person, troubled by stuffy air, has left a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone who has fled their homeland, an exile.

clue.text: Sacrifice one companion crossing second lake

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the companion stretches across the next letters, holding them

parts.note: a mate is a companion
mo is a moment, a second
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a friend while crossing a lake for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the brief moment, as in 'wait a mo', not an ordinal.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as a sacrifice, especially by burning.

clue.text: Potty at Balmoral perhaps causes rash

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy, mad
a Balmoral is a Scottish brimless cap, here one worn at the castle

explanation.surface: A chamber pot at the royal Scottish estate leads to a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' is not a child's toilet but slang for crazy, and a Balmoral is a flat Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes reckless, impulsive behaviour, so it means rash.

clue.text: Being less than generous with the Stilton?

definitions.text: Being less than generous with the Stilton?

parts.words: Being less than generous with the Stilton?
parts.note: shaving the thinnest possible slivers off a hunk of English blue, the literal picture of a stingy habit

explanation.walkthrough: Stilton is an English blue cheese; read literally, shaving thin slivers off it describes the miserly trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stingy or penny-pinching, literally the shaving of rinds and scraps.

clue.text: Capable Conservative means to apply pressure

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the UK party
a lever is a tool for applying force

explanation.surface: A competent Tory has ways to lean on people.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever means able and skilful, close to capable.

clue.text: Spoil lost princess's appearance?

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana, who died in 1997
figure is bodily shape or appearance

explanation.surface: Asks whether a missing princess's looks are ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: The princess is Diana, known as Di.
explanation.definitionFit: To disfigure is to spoil the look of something, mar it.

clue.text: Revolutionary payment method for strike-breaker

indicators.note: turning right round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: BACS is the UK automated bank clearing system for direct payments

explanation.surface: A radical new way of paying for a strike-breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British bank transfer system used for wages and bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike, derogatory slang for a blackleg.

clue.text: Place is an eyesore reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so sound matters not spelling

parts.note: a sight is something ugly, as in 'you look a sight'

explanation.surface: Somewhere said to be ugly to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot of ground, a place.

clue.text: See 22
Final race, say, under arc lights for starters

parts.note: a race is an example of a sporting event

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A final race run under floodlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means happening at last, ultimately resulting, so final.
